To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
overexpression of SOD1 in Drosophilla motorneurons extends lifespan, and that this is due to increased resistance to oxidative stress.
overexpression of SOD1 in the Drosophila nervous system, but not in other tissues, extends lifespan and that the extension of lifespan is dependent upon SOD activity.
overexpression of SOD1 in Drosophla motorneurons extends normal lifespan and rescues the short lifespan of Sod null mutants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of motorneurons and the role of reactive oxygen species in ageing and lifespan.
the role of oxidative stress in ageing and lifespan.
the role of motorneurons as a determinant of ageing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
overexpression of SOD in Drosophla motorneurons can increase lifespan and this is due to increased resistance to oxidative damage.
overexpression of human CuZnSOD (hSOD) in motorneurons of Drosophlia extends lifespan.

the lifespan of Drosophilla is increased when human SOD1 is overexpressed in motorneurons, and that the lifespan of a mutant lacking the endogenous SOD1 is restored by overexpression of the human enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lifespan of Drosophlia can be extended by overexpression of a human gene, CuZn superoxidase dismutase (human SOD1) in the adult motorneuron.
the motorneuron-specific overexpression of SOD1 in Drosophlia extends lifespan by 20-40%.
the lifespan of a fly is determined in part by the oxidative damage that occurs specifically in the motorneuron.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lifespan can be extended by overexpressing a single gene, superoxide dismutise, in a single type of cell, a motor neuron.
the lifespan of Drosophlia can be extended through the overexpression of SOD1 in the motor neurons of the organism.
the lifespan of the whole animal can be extended by increasing SOD activity in a single cell-type.
